svg.text: Your licence, and what to do the moment you make a mistake
Staying on the register
PIN for nurses and midwives; AIN for
nurse assistants.
Valid 12 months. Renew by 31 January.
CPD each year: Assistants 10 credits,
Staff to Officer 15, Senior Officer,
Tutor and above 20.
Notify the Registrar of a name or address change.
Practising on a lapsed PIN
Is an offence under section 73(d) of the
Health Professions Regulatory Bodies
Every shift worked without a valid PIN is
unregistered practice, however competent
the nurse and however short the ward is.
Your employer's rota is not a licence.
What the Council can do if misconduct is proved
Reprimand · Suspend from practice · Remove the name from the register · Postpone the order on conditions
The Disciplinary Committee inquires; the practitioner may attend, be represented, and appeal.
A name removed from the register may later be restored on application to the Council.
Suspension is not the end of the profession. Concealment usually is.
You have made an error — the order that protects the patient and you
1. Check and treat the patient first. Observations, then whatever the specific error requires.
2. Tell the prescriber or the person in charge straight away. Speed limits the harm.
3. Record what happened factually in the notes, and complete an incident form.
4. Be open with the patient and the family about what occurred and what is being done.
Patient, then prescriber, then paper. Never paper first, and never nothing at all.
Never alter or erase an entry. Rule a single line through it, write the correction, then sign, date and time it.
